- If sentiment is consistently low or neutral, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment history includes positive signals (e.g., >0.20), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast growth rate by 10–15% if sentiment is rising.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often fails to capture seasonal or policy-driven mean reversion; apply a 2–5% downward correction if recent 7-day average is above 75% of 30d mean.
- If sentiment is negative or volatile, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for 3–5 days if sentiment is below 0.10.
- Model often underestimates true volatility in early 30d forecasts; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
